title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 4-6). L is a set and Phi ⊂ P(L) is an 'admissible' family of subsets. Every x in S = |Phi| (the union of Phi) has a smallest member A(x) of Phi containing it. Each open stratum A° (A minus the members of Phi strictly contained in it) is nonempty. Equivalently, Phi is the data of a poset I ≅ Phi (ordered by inclusion) and a surjection phi: S → I, x ↦ A(x). Give I the Alexandrov-type topology: closed sets are the down-sets (unions of I_{≤i}), open sets are the up-sets (unions of I_{≥i}). Give S the inverse-image topology. Then A_i is the closure of the fibre phi^{-1}(i), i.e. A_i = phi^{-1}(I_{≤i}). The previous page shows that closed subsets of S are the sets A_J = ∪_{i∈J} A_i = ⊔_{i∈J} A_i°, for J a down-set.

This page continues the dictionary.
(1) Open subsets of S are the sets A_J = phi^{-1}(J) = ∪_{i∈J} A_i°, for J an up-set (open) of I. Grothendieck remarks, as a 'chose curieuse', that here one cannot replace A_i° by A_i, unlike the closed case. Indeed, the union of the closed strata over an up-set J is the closure-saturation of phi^{-1}(J), not phi^{-1}(J) itself.
(2) Locally closed subsets of S are the sets phi^{-1}(J), for J locally closed in I. These are exactly the order-convex subsets: (*) i ≤ j ≤ k with i, k ∈ J implies j ∈ J. Proof sketch: the up-sets I_{≥i}, i ∈ J, form an open cover of J. By (*), J ∩ I_{≥i} is closed in I_{≥i}, so J is locally closed. The converse is 'even more evident', since open ∩ closed = up-set ∩ down-set is convex.
(3) NB, for Phi finite: the open strata A° are the atoms of the Boolean subalgebra of P(S) generated by Phi. The generated Boolean algebra (finite unions, intersections, complements in S) consists exactly of the subsets saturated for the equivalence relation R_Phi defined by phi, i.e. unions of strata. Hence it is in bijection with P(I) via J ↦ phi^{-1}(J) = ∪_{i∈J} A_i°. These sets are named 'Phi-measurable / Phi-constructible'.

Purpose: this is the elementary combinatorial-topological groundwork of an 'algebra of figures'. It encodes a stratified set by its poset of closed strata and identifies closed, open, locally closed and constructible sets with down-sets, up-sets, convex sets and arbitrary subsets of the poset. This prepares sub-families (p. 6: closed sub-families ↔ saturated |Psi|).
errors: No genuine error. The finiteness hypothesis in the NB is needed and correctly added: for infinite Phi, the fibres A_i° = A_i minus the union of the smaller A_j need not lie in the Boolean algebra generated by finite operations, and that algebra is not all of P(I). The atom claim itself holds because x ∈ A_j iff phi(x) ≤ j, so the membership pattern of x determines phi(x) and conversely.
The proof of 'convex implies locally closed' is only sketched (and partly illegible), but it is correct.

ideas.what: Open, closed and locally closed sets of the Alexandrov topology of a poset are the up-sets, down-sets and order-convex sets; these are transported to a stratified set via the stratum map phi.
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology / poset-stratified spaces (locally closed = convex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. S. Alexandrov (1937); standard in stratified-space theory (e.g. Lurie HA Appendix A, Curry, MacPherson exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Constructible sets and the 'specialization order' appear in EGA 0_III/IV, but not in this poset form as far as I know

ideas.what: For finite Phi, the open strata are the atoms of the Boolean algebra generated by Phi, and Phi-constructible sets correspond to arbitrary subsets of I.
ideas.modern_name: Atoms of a finitely generated Boolean algebra of sets; constructible sets as unions of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Boole/Stone); analogous to EGA's constructible sets
ideas.where_published: Analogy with EGA IV §1 (constructible sets), not this statement

ideas.what: Remark that open sets are unions of open strata over up-sets, but cannot be written as unions of closed strata.
ideas.modern_name: Asymmetry between open and closed unions in a stratification

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary groundwork: the dictionary between stratified sets and posets with the Alexandrov topology, plus a finite Boolean-algebra remark. Interest is mainly historical, as part of Grothendieck's 1986 'algèbre des figures' (possibly related to his tame-topology programme). There is nothing mathematically new for a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'où J est une partie ouverte de I (muni de la top. ..., Φ ≃ I)'.
'Les parties loc. fermées sont de la forme' is probably 'Les parties loc. fermées sont de même la forme'.

In the parenthetical proof, read: 'J ∩ I_{≥i} est fermé dans I_{≥i} à cause de (*), et pour un tel recouvrement ouvert, J est [loc.] fermé ... donc J est bien loc. fermé si (*), l'inv. étant encore plus évident'.
The final line probably reads 'les parties Φ-mesurables ou Φ-constructibles de S' (or '... de |Φ|') rather than 'Φ-modulaires ... de Φ'.
'atomes [?]' is confirmed: 'les atomes de l'algèbre de Boole engendrée par les A∈Φ'.
